stories.title: She Rolls Gaming Initiative Invites The Girlies To Play Dungeons & Dragons
stories.summary: Katarina Merlini's She Rolls Initiative is making Dungeons & Dragons accessible for women, femmes, and gender-expansive gamers. The beginner-friendly event sold out in a week, packing 95 people into a sports bar. It's all about creating a welcoming space for those who've felt on the fringes of tabletop gaming.
stories.extended_summary: When Katarina Merlini booked Babe's Sports Bar for her inclusive D&D night, she worried it would feel too empty. Instead, 95 people signed up within a week, proving there's a huge appetite for gaming spaces that welcome women, femmes, and gender-expansive folks. The sold-out event, powered by 15 volunteers, is part of a bigger push to expand tabletop gaming access across the Midwest. Merlini's already planning a second event — the girlies are here to play.

stories.title: The IP Moat: How Sahara Lotti Built and Defended Lashify
stories.summary: Sahara Lotti turned a personal beauty problem into Lashify, a $8 million business in its first year. She built a patent fortress with over 700 global patents and won a landmark $30.5 million legal victory against copycats. Her story shows how protecting your ideas can build generational wealth.
stories.extended_summary: Sahara Lotti started Lashify with $300 and a frustration: no at-home lash extensions existed. She invented the category, grew it to $8 million in year one, and then defended it fiercely. With 700+ patents and a $30.5 million court win against overseas manufacturers, Lotti turned intellectual property into a moat. Her journey is a masterclass in building and protecting a brand in a copycat industry.

stories.title: The why behind sex
stories.summary: Harvard biologists used yeast to uncover why sexual reproduction exists. In just four months, they watched 960 generations evolve and found that sex helps organisms adapt to changing environments. It's a fast-forward look at evolution that explains one of biology's biggest mysteries.
stories.extended_summary: Why do we have sex? It's costly and inefficient, yet it dominates life on Earth. Harvard researchers used yeast — which can reproduce both ways — to watch evolution happen in real time. Over 960 generations, they saw how sexual reproduction gives species a survival edge when environments shift. This isn't just biology trivia; it's a window into the very engine of life's diversity.

stories.extended_summary: Diana Stelin's double-sided flag — Venice on one side, Burano on the other — will float in the Venetian lagoon, slowly transformed by wind, water, and algae. It's her second year at the Biennale, and the piece is a love letter to her Brookline community, from the bold colors of her young students to the local Italian connections. Stelin's gallery has evolved into a 'creativity hub' that blends art, education, and community. Now, that hub is going global.
